text:
GruntWorx should inherit Instead’s reliability patterns, while keeping vendor-specific limits, statuses and matching rules in its own adapter.

1. **Rate limits need two budgets.** Instead throttles each API group **per connection**, plus the whole application. The group check runs first so a rejected job does not consume the application budget. Defaults are 500 requests/minute application-wide and 5/minute for documents; production config raises these to 3,000 and 60. GruntWorx needs its own negotiated values and bucket keys. Honor `Retry-After` as seconds or an HTTP date, and expose remaining/reset metrics. Operations normally allow **10 retries**, roughly 4½ hours on Sidekiq’s ladder, but throttle rescheduling resets the count—this is **not a wall-clock deadline**.  
   Sources: [throttle](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/config/initializers/sidekiq.rb:101), [production limits](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/config/settings/production.yml:187), [retry policy](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/operation_worker.rb:10).

2. **Webhooks need bounded reconciliation.** The sweep is designed to run every **30 minutes**, selecting uploaded documents still `sent` after **1 hour** or `processing` after **12 hours**, and stopping eligibility after **2 days**. Those thresholds can vary by provider; older records remain unchanged. Instead groups reads by entity/year, follows folder pagination, then individually fetches candidates absent from every page. An individual document’s 404 becomes `archived`; a missing/forbidden folder is skipped. Page jobs have no automatic retries; another sweep can retry while the document remains eligible. GruntWorx should preserve this recovery mechanism and make its recovery window explicit.  
   Sources: [candidate windows](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/queries/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_candidates_query.rb:8), [pagination and fallback](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/reconcile_statuses_worker.rb:24), [individual lookup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/reconcile_status.rb:38).

3. **Keep one internal failure vocabulary and one status writer.** Shared reasons are `unexpected`, `no_active_connection`, `network_error`, `unauthorized`, `api_error`, `exceeded`, `forbidden`, and `encrypted`. Vendor adapters translate into them: Instead maps `password_required` to `encrypted`; unknown indexing reasons produce `error` without an invented reason. Both webhooks and reconciliation use `ApplyProcessingStatus`, which ignores repeated states and handles recovery from `error` to `processed` transactionally through `processing`. Separate terminal refusals from retryable failures; **quota exhaustion and HTTP 429 are different cases**.  
   Sources: [shared vocabulary](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:12), [refusal classification](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/refusals_helper.rb:8), [status translation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/apply_processing_status.rb:8).

4. **Signed-upload cassettes need safe recording and faithful replay.** The global recording hook scrubs policy, credential, signature and client-secret fields from request/response bodies while preserving payload shape. Instead bearer/token scrubbing is host-specific, so GruntWorx authentication needs corresponding coverage. Tagged cassette replay freezes time at the recording timestamp so expiring upload targets remain reproducible; new recordings use the real clock. Preserve expiry validation, multipart field order and the separate upload transport that sends no vendor bearer grant to storage.  
   Sources: [recording hook](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/spec_helper.rb:164), [replay clock](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/support/vcr_fixed_time.rb:3), [upload transport](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/base_client.rb:243).

5. **Entity matching should prefer durable identity and abstain on ambiguity.** Instead first reuses a stored taxpayer/type link across tax years, then tries a unique unlinked entity from the local sync, and creates remotely only when neither succeeds. Matching stays within firm and entity type. It normalizes punctuation, whitespace and case; business matching also normalizes legal-form spellings. Personal matching tries reversed first/last names only after no direct match, and uses the account name only for a sole contact. Multiple matches remain unlinked and emit an ambiguity outcome. GruntWorx should retain those safeguards, adapting the identity fields to its contract. Remote entity creation is explicitly **non-idempotent**, making stored handles especially important.  
   Sources: [selection order](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/export_async_workflow.rb:23), [matching rules](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/link_entity_by_name.rb:14), [creation and identity](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/create_entity.rb:3).

These are lessons supported by the existing code; GruntWorx’s actual API guarantees still need verification. No files were edited.
